# Phase 9 prompt — Complete release verification and migrate documentation

Implement only Phase 9 of the Unfinished Business roadmap. This is the release-quality gate: reconcile implementation and documentation, run the complete verification matrix, archive superseded material safely, and prepare an evidence-backed handoff. Do not add substantial new features during this phase.

## Prerequisite

Verify Phases 0–8 are either complete or explicitly scoped out by an approved decision. A missing MUST behavior is a blocker, not documentation work to hide.

## Outcome

The repository has one coherent product story, canonical and accurate setup/architecture/operations documentation, tested local and hosted-demo paths, a reviewable private-hosted procedure, complete evidence, and no unidentified worktree changes.

## Reconcile implementation first

- Inspect repository instructions, branch/HEAD, full worktree status, recent phase commits/handoffs, manifests, generated assets, source, tests, deployment configuration, and every active document.
- Build a requirements-to-evidence matrix for Maker reliability, OpenCode onboarding/controls, navigation, landing/theme, recommendations, modes, demo, security, accessibility, and documentation.
- Classify every item as verified, failed, unavailable, deferred by approved decision, or blocked. Do not convert missing proof into a pass.
- Fix release-blocking defects and documentation mismatches only. Route material new features back to the relevant phase.

## Full verification matrix

Run and record:

- clean dependency install where safe and reproducible;
- typecheck, full unit/integration tests, production build, and dependency audit;
- state migration from supported prior schema fixtures;
- Maker queue/events/reconnect/restart/interrupt/unknown-outcome matrix;
- OpenCode authentication, discovery, unavailable model/provider, permissions, and session controls using deterministic tests plus an authorized live smoke test when available;
- local fresh setup and main journey;
- hosted demo journey with proof of no inference/repository mutation;
- static Render/private-host validation and live deployment only if separately authorized;
- four-stage navigation and approval-gate regression;
- deterministic demo and reset isolation;
- recommendation policy fixtures and source freshness;
- keyboard, focus, reduced motion, contrast, text zoom, narrow/wide layout, overflow, and relevant screen-reader semantics;
- security, redaction, retention, backup, corruption, SSRF/path, origin, and rate-limit tests;
- bundle/asset performance budgets;
- Sentry release/source-map/trace checks only in environments with authorized credentials.

Capture command, revision, environment, result, and limitation. Do not publish secrets, private transcripts, or unrestricted local paths in evidence.

## Documentation requirements and migration

Make these canonical and accurate:

- `README.md`
- `docs/PRODUCT_BRIEF.md`
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`
- `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`
- `docs/OPENCODE_INTEGRATION.md`
- `docs/LOCAL_SETUP.md`
- `docs/HOSTED_DEPLOYMENT.md`
- `docs/TOOL_CATALOG.md`
- `docs/UX_AND_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md`
- `docs/OPERATIONS_AND_RECOVERY.md`
- `docs/DEMO_AND_SUBMISSION.md`
- `docs/DECISIONS.md`
- `docs/CHANGELOG.md`

Then:

- Compare legacy documents against canonical content line by line for unique facts and provenance.
- Move genuinely superseded documents into `docs/history/` using Git-aware moves when possible.
- Add a short superseded notice and pointer where stable incoming links may still matter.
- Do not archive the four runtime stage prompts. If they are renamed to clearer names, update loaders, tests, links, provenance, and migration notes atomically:
  - `ORACLE_PRODUCT_DISCOVERY.md`
  - `ARCHITECT_ENGINEERING_PLAN.md`
  - `MAKER_BUILD_AND_VERIFY.md`
  - `WITNESS_DEMO_AND_SUBMISSION.md`
- Keep this implementation prompt pack separate from runtime prompt discovery.
- Remove obsolete active claims, duplicated setup steps, stale model constants, and dead links.
- Add document status/owner/last-verified metadata where it improves maintenance.
- Ensure every user-visible behavior has a setup, operation, recovery, or limitation reference.

## Release and submission handoff

- Prepare a concise release note from the changelog.
- Create an evidence index linking screenshots, demo script, test reports, architecture diagram, OpenCode proof, and selected partner proof.
- Verify challenge/category claims against actual meaningful usage. Do not claim a partner category for installation alone.
- Keep publication, submission, deployment, domain registration, credit claiming, account changes, and public transcript sharing pending unless explicitly authorized.
- Record known limitations and post-release work, especially shared multi-user hosting and remote browser-to-local pairing.

## Acceptance

- All MUST requirements have current evidence or the release is explicitly blocked.
- Canonical docs match implemented routes, schemas, environment variables, versions, modes, and UI terminology.
- Legacy material is preserved under history or deliberately retained with an ownership note; no unique user decision is lost.
- Runtime prompts and implementation prompts cannot be confused by loaders or users.
- Local setup is reproducible; hosted demo is safe and truthful; private hosting steps are reviewable.
- No secrets/private traces are in tracked files or public evidence.
- Full tests/build pass and the worktree contains no unidentified changes.

Finish with the required phase handoff. Report `BUILD_COMPLETE — READY_FOR_FINAL_REVIEW` only when every release criterion is actually satisfied. Do not deploy, publish, push, or submit without separate explicit authorization.
I'll start by inspecting the repository state, instructions, and phase handoffs before making any changes.

54: 
55: Primary user: a first-time hackathon builder or developer using AI who struggles with what to ask, which tool capability to choose, how to carry decisions between sessions, and how to know when the result is actually ready.

62:

The companion clarifies one useful journey, recommends a manageable scope, explains a proposed plan, asks for approval, guides a real bounded implementation, and records what verification observed. On return, the student sees where work stopped and which approvals still apply.

# Unfinished Business

**Turn unfinished ideas into hackathon-ready builds.**

Unfinished Business is an OpenCode-powered hackathon project builder. Four friendly spirits guide one idea through a clear proposal, an approved plan, a real bounded build, and evidence you can defend.

![Ghostlight Hacker Workshop landing page](tests/visual/snapshots/landing-wide.png)

## What it is

- A **landing page** at `/` that explains the product, the four roles, OpenCode's role, and the two honest usage paths.
- A **guided deterministic example** at `/demo`: a versioned Campus Umbrella Relay fixture with Play/Pause, step, replay, reset, four inspectable spirit tabs, a representative diff and check, Witness findings, and an optional 90-second presentation mode at `/demo?presentation=1`. It does not call a model or read a repository.
- The **real workshop** at `/workshop`, which connects to a local OpenCode server and records what actually happened.
- A **first-run connection and discovery flow** that checks a supported OpenCode server, lists the models/providers/agents it actually reports, and lets the builder choose a model and reported reasoning variant. Provider API keys stay inside OpenCode.

OpenCode supplies the agent loop, model access, native tools, permissions, execution, interruption, and native sessions. Unfinished Business adds the four-stage workshop, exact-version approvals, dependency invalidation, evidence views, the onboarding/discovery flow, and the Ghostlight interface. It does **not** ship a second coding harness or a general command executor.

| Spirit | Role |
|---|---|
| Oracle | Clarify an idea into a product proposal and open questions |
| Architect | Draft one planning section and wait for approval of that exact version |
| Maker | Perform an approved, bounded native edit through OpenCode |
| Witness | Inspect evidence in a fresh session and prepare honest review drafts |

## Two ways to use it

**Hosted demo or private deployment** — a labeled deterministic sample, or a private, password-protected workshop using the server's own isolated demo workspace. It does not reach into a visitor's local repository, and it is not a public execution sandbox.

**Full local mode** — the browser app, local API, and pinned OpenCode server on your machine over loopback. Maker's edit in this release is bounded to an isolated demo workspace. App approval never overrides an OpenCode permission denial.

`UB_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` selects `local`, `hosted-private`, or `hosted-demo`. Local mode can edit the connection and enter the server password in memory. Hosted-private manages the URL/credentials in the environment and keeps browser configuration read-only. Hosted-demo serves the guided fixture, issues no session token, connects to no OpenCode server, and rejects every non-GET `/api/*` request with `DEMO_READ_ONLY`.

The landing page exposes three distinct actions: **Try the example** (`/demo`), **Watch the guided workflow** (`/demo?presentation=1`), and **Run live with OpenCode** (`/workshop`). The example is always labeled as a prerecorded fixture; the live native session remains `NOT_RUN`.

Models are discovered from OpenCode rather than assumed. The free DeepSeek route, `opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`, was the intended development route and is still listed by the tested server, but its availability is time-limited and must be verified on your own account. No paid fallback is configured.

## Quick start

Prerequisites: Linux, Node **22.14+**, npm, and a supported OpenCode 2.x server. Copying `.env.example` to `.env` is optional for local work; the first-run wizard can hold the server password in memory.

```bash
npm ci
cp .env.example .env   # optional
```

Terminal 1 — OpenCode:

```bash
./node_modules/@opencode/cli-linux-x64-baseline/bin/opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4096
```

Terminal 2 — API:

```bash
npm run dev
```

Terminal 3 — interface:

```bash
npm run dev:web
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:5173/`. The first-run wizard asks for the server URL and the password printed by `opencode serve`; provider accounts are connected inside OpenCode with `/connect`, and the model list comes from OpenCode's catalog.

For a single production process:

```bash
npm run build
npm start
```

Then open `http://127.0.0.1:4200/`. The detailed, tested guide is [docs/LOCAL_SETUP.md](docs/LOCAL_SETUP.md).

## Phase 8 — security, persistence, and operations hardening

### Added

- Explicit `local`, `hosted-demo`, and `private-hosted` modes with fail-closed startup validation.
- Canonical workspace roots, broad-root rejection, traversal/symlink/special-file checks, private file/directory permissions, and static-file containment.
- Safe OpenCode transport: URL syntax policy, loopback default, HTTPS/allowlist for remote targets, per-request DNS/IP validation, metadata/private-address blocking, redirect refusal, request timeout, and response-size cap.
- OpenCode readiness gate for version 2.x, authentication, and the required free DeepSeek model before mutation.
- Host allowlist, Origin/`Sec-Fetch-Site` checks, constant-time session token, Basic Auth in hosted modes, JSON/content-type enforcement, request-size cap, per-client rate limit, mutation concurrency gate, and bounded authenticated SSE.
- Atomic state schema v2 with `createdAt`/`updatedAt`, mode/demo metadata, v1 migration, backup rotation, corrupt quarantine, cross-process lock, disk-full/read-only mapping, and startup recovery for in-flight operations.
- Centralized redaction for state, exports, errors, structured logs, and Sentry payloads; independent redaction tests.
- Configurable guide/Maker/Node-check timeouts, session token/cost budgets, visible provider-data limitation, retention policies, and structured correlation-ID logs.
- `GET /api/runtime` for mode/demo/limits/retention visibility; `GET /api/events` authenticated SSE snapshots.
- Security/recovery tests for traversal, symlink escape, unsafe roots, SSRF/DNS/redirect/size/timeout, Origin/CORS/CSRF, SSE auth, cross-operation access, request/rate/concurrency limits, duplicate actions, redaction, corrupt state, disk failure, restart, unknown outcomes, budgets, and retention.
- Documentation: architecture/trust boundaries, operations/recovery, OpenCode integration, local setup, hosted deployment, UX/visual system, decisions, implementation plan.

### Changed

- `project.json` schema is now v2 (`schemaVersion: 2`); v1 snapshots migrate on read.
- `/api/project`, `/api/export`, `/api/engine`, and `/api/runtime` now require the session token; hosted modes additionally require Basic Auth.
- `/api/project` omits the persisted workspace path from browser responses.
- The guide no longer silently re-prompts after a short native reply; one request has one possible side effect.
- Maker timeouts/permission waits become `UNKNOWN`/`WAITING_PERMISSION` and cannot be retried automatically.
- Cancellation attempts a native interrupt and refuses to mark cancelled when interruption fails.
- Retained approvals/actions/operations/transcripts/evidence/drafts are bounded.
- Local mode no longer emits HSTS; hosted modes still do.
- Structured JSON logs replace ad-hoc startup error output in the server/render entry points.

- Unused `src/server/opencode/operations.ts` helper and its test (no production references).

- Shared-host isolation is not provided. The demo workspace and native permissions reduce scope, but the Node check is not an OS sandbox.
